newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: Papua New Guinea MP kidnapped on Bougainville.
newsitem.headline: Papua New Guinea MP kidnapped on Bougainville.

text.p: A Papua New Guinea member of parliament has been kidnapped while campaigning for national elections on the secessionist island of Bougainville, the Papua New Guinea government said on Monday.
John Momis, the member for Bougainville in the national parliament, was abducuted on Sunday by members of the Bougainville Revolutionary Army (BRA), the government said.
A member of his staff was taken with him at from Tinputz, a regional centre on north Bougainville, it said.
Momis is a strong supporter of the Papua New Guinea government on the issue of Bougainville, where rebels have been fighting a successionist war for nine years.
The BRA has said previously it plans to disrupt national elections, which are due to begin June 14.
Bougainville came to international attention earlier this year when an army revolt stymied government plans to use merceneries to put an end to the uprising.
Acting Prime Minister John Giheno last week unveiled a surprise plan aimed at peacefully ending the rebellion, in which thousands have died, mainly from disease.
Giheno said the South Pacific nation now believed there could be no military solution to the conflict. The rebels have made no official response to the peace offer.
